scope: Generic WIC controls, electrical, pump-down, room/load/infiltration. Exact wiring, settings and motor/compressor limits remain equipment-specific.
principles: Electrical troubleshooting follows the control path: demand -> controller/thermostat -> safeties -> contactor/relay -> load, using the actual wiring diagram.
No-voltage-at-load and correct-voltage-but-load-will-not-run are different diagnostic branches.
A safety control opening is evidence of a condition or control fault, not automatically a defective safety.
Pump-down is a sequence; low suction is expected after the liquid solenoid closes until the LP control stops the compressor.
Room temperature failure must be separated into load/infiltration, airflow, refrigeration capacity/feed, controls/sensors, and sizing.
Sensor location/calibration and controller settings can mimic refrigeration faults.
Do not invent universal voltage/current, LP/HP, thermostat differential, anti-short-cycle, or pump-down settings.

domains.condition: Cooling is expected but compressor is not operating.
branches: no voltage at compressor: trace upstream through disconnect/fuse/wiring/contactor/safeties/controller
voltage present at compressor but no start: verify voltage under start attempt, motor/start components/protection/model requirements
safety open: determine whether pressure/oil/overload condition is real before condemning control
domains.diagnosis_policy: Use wiring diagram and voltage/state evidence to localize interruption; do not jump directly to compressor failure.

domains.condition: Commanded load does not match controller/relay/contactor output.
domains.diagnosis_policy: Separate missing command, failed coil, failed contacts and downstream load fault.

domains.condition: Controller action is inconsistent with actual room/system condition.
domains.diagnosis_policy: A bad room temperature does not by itself prove refrigeration-circuit failure.

domains.condition: Thermostat/controller satisfies and liquid solenoid closes; compressor continues until LP control cut-out, then restarts when demand/pressure logic permits.
expected_sequence: LP control opens at configured cut-out
on new demand solenoid opens and suction rises
LP control closes at configured cut-in and compressor starts, subject to delays/safeties
faults: refrigerant migration/pressure rise causing unwanted cycling
domains.diagnosis_policy: Compare actual sequence with equipment wiring/control design; do not infer low charge merely from intentional low suction during pump-down.

domains.condition: Heat/moisture load exceeds expected operating load or repeatedly enters room.
discriminators: product load and entering product temperature
refrigeration system performance under known load
domains.diagnosis_policy: Do not call system undersized until correct operation and actual/design load are compared.

domains.condition: System operates correctly but cannot meet actual/design room load.
domains.diagnosis_policy: Sizing is a late-stage conclusion requiring load/equipment data, not a fallback diagnosis.
